assumptions_made: Used log-normal distributions to simulate skewed data since the original dataset didn't provide suitable skewed distributions
Generated synthetic data with fixed seed for reproducibility
Used 1000 samples per replicate to balance computational efficiency with statistical stability
Used 1000 bootstrap resamples to ensure stable confidence interval estimation
Used 100 replicates per skewness level to get stable coverage estimates
Used the percentile bootstrap method as specified in the literature
Set the true median for log-normal(0,σ) to 1.0 (which is correct)
Used 95% confidence intervals as specified in the hypothesis
Used a tolerance of 0.03 around the nominal 95% coverage as specified in success criteria
The Hugging Face dataset was not suitable for this experiment due to lack of appropriate skewed distributions, so synthetic data was generated instead
The synthetic data generation creates realistic ranges and correlation structures for the bootstrap experiment

results.hypothesis: Test whether the bootstrap confidence interval for a median achieves nominal coverage on skewed data.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: The nominal 95% coverage the interval claims.
results.success_criteria: Empirical coverage stays within 0.03 of nominal at every skewness level.
results.notes:
Skewness 0.0: coverage 1.000 differs from nominal 0.95 by 0.050 (> 0.03)
